# Speccify 0.13.1 for Windows

Speccify brings Specs, project knowledge, terminals and a configurable development
process into one workspace. Use your own CLI and account, and share questions,
answers and review requests through the project's Git-backed Message Board.

Configure process steps with imported methods, column titles and colors. Start
steps deliberately from a Spec; moving a card does not start a CLI. Questions and
results stay linked to their Spec across devices. Paired work requests require
the receiving device's explicit permission for the sender and exact action.

This Windows release corrects the first Terminal's startup. Its host completes
the Windows console handshake before a view attaches. New project views provide
Notes and a working Terminal. Updates preserve existing sessions; when an older
host is retained, a new project explains how to create its Terminal explicitly.

Resource cards can be dragged from the Navigator into the bottom area or the
lower Inspector in the Process main window. Windows now uses the same internal
drag-and-drop handling there as in project windows.

The regular package keeps the existing application identity and update channel.
New profiles start with Process. Existing full-workspace profiles retain their
interface until a guarded change in Settings. Earlier Basic installations have
a separate compatibility installer that preserves their own identity and profile.

For regular Windows installations from 0.11.0 or earlier, download and run
the matching installer once; the old update button may not offer this release.
The installation retains the existing profile and Stable/Beta preference.

Windows installers are not Authenticode-signed. Updater signatures are verified
separately. Some native menu and New Project labels remain English when German
is selected; workspace help is available in both languages.

This release contains Windows x64 packages only. macOS remains at the published
[0.13.0 release](https://github.com/mhennemeyer/speccify-releases/releases/tag/v0.13.0).
The [download page](https://speccify.io/download/) lists each platform's actual
published version and its matching setup guide.
